The tooltip parameter of any element (flow uses the area of an element without a name for you). gui.Tooltip can only be attached to a named element. field[name;label;default] A small form with a single field and an automatic "Proceed" button (for example for signs). Use a gui.Field and a gui.Button.

docs.title: Missing parameters
docs.text:
• Content padding of scroll containers. Luanti can work out the range of a scroll container's scrollbar for you, but flow's gui.ScrollContainer does not expose this, so you have to set the range yourself with gui.ScrollbarOptions. gui.ScrollableVBox already does this for you.
  • Node formspec inventory locations. The "current_node" inventory location refers to the node whose formspec is open. A flow form cannot be the formspec of a node, so use "nodemeta:X,Y,Z" to show a node's inventory instead.

docs.title: Things flow does for you
docs.text:
These formspec elements exist, but flow generates them itself and you cannot write them:

  • size[]: The size of the form is worked out from the elements in it.
  • position[], anchor[], and padding[]: Use the window_position, window_anchor, and window_padding options of the root element, see Window position.
  • no_prepend[] and bgcolor[]: Use the no_prepend option and the bgcolor, fbgcolor, and bg_fullscreen options of the root element.
  • real_coordinates[]: Flow always uses the newer coordinate system, where there is no hidden padding or spacing between elements.
  • container_end[] and scroll_container_end[]: Elements inside gui.Container and gui.ScrollContainer are written inside the table.
  • formspec_version[]: Flow always uses formspec version 7.

docs.title: Newer Luanti features
docs.text: Because flow always uses formspec version 7 (Luanti 5.8), features that were added in newer versions may not work, even if the missing element or parameter is not listed above. This includes the area label (version 9), floating-point animation frames in gui.Model (version 10), and the halign and valign styles of fields and text areas (version 11), and the editable style of checkboxes, dropdowns, and fields (version 12, the only addition in that version). Formspec versions are described in the "Formspec Version History" section of the Luanti API documentation.

docs.title: Formspec versions and Luanti releases
docs.text: Formspec version Luanti release Notable additions 2 5.1.0 Real coordinates always on, background9[] 3 5.2.0 Draw order follows definition order, scroll_container[] 4 5.4.0 Dropdown index events 5 5.5.0 padding[] 6 5.6.0 Nine-slice images, animated_image[] 7 5.8.0 Focused button state, field_enter_after_edit[] (the version flow uses) 8 5.10.0 Scroll container content padding 9 5.12.0 allow_close[], area label[] 10 5.13.0 Floating-point model[] frames 11 5.17.0 hypertip[], text alignment styles 12 5.18.0 editable style

docs.title: Padding, spacing, and backgrounds
docs.text:
Most elements can have a padding value, which will add the specified amount of padding around the element, measured in slot units. The "root" element of the form (the one returned by the build function) has a default padding of 0.3, everything else has a default padding of 0.

padding is ignored on these elements:

  • gui.Flow, gui.ScrollableVBox, and gui.PaginatedVBox. To pad one, put it inside a gui.VBox (or another layouting element) and set padding on that instead.
  • Elements inside a gui.Container, which are placed at their x and y and are not padded.
  • Invisible elements such as gui.Style, which take up no space.

There is also a deprecated gui.Padding element that wraps a single element and pads it. Use the padding parameter instead.

HBox and VBox have a spacing field which specifies how much spacing there is between elements inside the box. Its default value is described in gui.VBox.

Container elements (HBox and VBox) can optionally have bgimg and bgimg_middle parameters that specify a background for the container. bgimg is the name of a texture, which is stretched to fill the container. If bgimg_middle is set as well, the texture is drawn as a nine-slice whose corners are bgimg_middle pixels big, so one small texture can make a background of any size. The background will be drawn behind any padding that the container has.

Example with only bgimg:

gui.VBox {
    -- Stretch the texture over the whole box
    bgimg = "air.png",

    gui.Button { label = "Button 1" },
    gui.Button { label = "Button 2" },
}

Example with bgimg_middle as well:

gui.VBox {
    padding = 0.5,
    spacing = 0.1,

    -- Draw the texture as a nine-slice
    bgimg = "air.png",
    bgimg_middle = 2,

    gui.Button { label = "Button 1" },
    gui.Button { label = "Button 2" },
}

The padding around the VBox is 0.5 and the spacing between the buttons inside it is 0.1.

docs.title: Popovers (highly experimental)
docs.text:
This API will likely have breaking changes in the future.

Flow supports a highly experimental low-level API for defining popovers. Popovers appear over top of all other elements and are anchored to their parent.

This API is intended to be used for creating themed widgets like dropdowns, or for a higher level popover API that adds styling and is easier to use.

You add a popover attribute to any container element to define a popover. Flow does not manage the lifecycle (opening/closing) of popovers, you must ensure that you do this yourself like in the example.

Two parameters go on the container that owns the popover:

  • popover: the element to show over the container, or nil for no popover.
  • on_close_popover: a function that flow calls with (player, ctx) when the player clicks anywhere outside the popover. Like an on_event function, it can return true to redraw the form. Flow only adds this click catcher while a popover is shown.

See the below example for details on how to use the API. The popover is drawn from the build function, so it can depend on ctx:

local gui = flow.widgets

local my_gui = flow.make_gui(function(player, ctx)
    return gui.VBox {
        -- Some padding is added for the purposes of the demo so that the popup
        -- isn't off-screen
        padding = 3,
        gui.Label { label = "Popover demo:" },

        gui.Stack {
            gui.Button {
                label = "Open popover",

                -- When the popover button is clicked, open the popover
                on_event = function(player, ctx)
                    ctx.show_popover = true
                    return true
                end,
            },

            -- The actual element to overlay
            -- "popover" is set to the gui.VBox element if (and only if)
            -- ctx.show_popover is true, otherwise it's nil so no popover is
            -- shown.
            popover = ctx.show_popover and gui.VBox {
                -- Specifying padding and bgcolor is optional, but is probably
                -- a good idea since flow doesn't do any styling on its own.
                padding = 0.2,
                bgcolor = "#222e",

                -- "side" specifies how the popover is positioned relative to
                -- the parent, and can be "bottom" (default), "top", "left", or
                -- "right". It is nil on the first draw, which means "bottom".
                side = ctx.form.side,

                -- align_h and align_v align the popover according to its
                -- parent element. You only need to specify align_h for
                -- side = "top"/"bottom" or align_v for side = "left"/"right",
                -- this example specifies both so that it can demonstrate
                -- switching between different sides.
                align_h = "fill",
                align_v = "center",

                -- Popover contents
                gui.Label { label = "Hi there!" },
                gui.Dropdown {
                    name = "side",
                    items = {
                        "bottom",
                        "top",
                        "left",
                        "right",
                    },
                },
            } or nil,

            -- Clicking outside the popover will call this function, which
            -- should probably close the popover.
            on_close_popover = function(player, ctx)
                ctx.show_popover = false
                return true
            end,
        },

        gui.Label { label = "After popover button" },
    }
end)

Show the form with my_gui:show(player) as usual.

align_h and align_v are among the parameters shared by all elements.

There are some restrictions on popovers:

  • They must not extend outside the form, otherwise they'll only be partially visible (unless everything is styled with noclip = true). Flow does not attempt to detect this.
  • You can only define popover on container elements, like gui.Stack, gui.HBox, and gui.VBox.
  • Only one popover is shown at a time.
  • Players can still use tab to interact with things behind the popover, despite being unable to use their mouse to do so.
  • You cannot show popovers inside of other popovers.
  • Popovers cannot be on the root element.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: A player's client can send anything to the server. A normal client only sends values that the form could produce, but a modified one can send other names, other values, and several actions at once. This page lists what flow checks before it stores a value or calls one of your functions, and what it leaves to you.

docs.title: What flow checks
docs.text:
• The form. Flow only handles input for the form that the player has open right now. Every time a form is shown with form:show() it gets a new internal name, so input that is meant for an old or made-up form is ignored.
  • The elements. Flow only stores values for named inputs that were in the form it drew, and only calls on_event and on_key_enter functions of elements that were in it. Anything else the client sends is ignored. Hidden elements are not part of the form, see Hiding elements.
  • Size. A value longer than 60,000 bytes is ignored and a warning is logged.
  • Text. Control characters other than tabs and newlines are removed from the text of gui.Field, gui.Pwdfield, and gui.Textarea, and from the value of a gui.Hypertext action. The same goes for the control characters from U+0080 to U+009F. Newlines are also removed from gui.Field, where a player can only enter one by pasting it.
  • Checkboxes. The value is always true or false.
  • Dropdowns. The value must be one of the items. With index_event = true it must be a number from 1 to the number of items. On clients that support it, flow always asks for the item number instead of the text, so the client never gets to choose the text.
  • Tabs, tables, and text lists. The selected tab or row must be a number from 1 to the number of tabs or rows. Decimals are rounded down.
  • Buttons. Flow calls the on_event function of at most one button per submission, and not at the same time as an on_key_enter function. Buttons never store a value.

When a value is rejected, ctx.form keeps its previous value. The other values in the same submission are still used.

docs.title: What you still need to check
docs.text:
• Who is allowed to do something. Flow can tell that a button exists in the form, but not whether the player really clicked it. A modified client can trigger the on_event function of any element that is currently in the form. Check privileges, ownership, distances and so on inside the function, the same as you would in a chat command.
  • What is in the value. Flow does not limit text to a length (apart from 60,000 bytes), and it does not check scrollbar positions against the range of the scrollbar. Check values that matter before you use them, for example before putting text into a node's metadata.
  • Inventories. The slots of a gui.List are handled by Luanti, flow does not check or limit what is moved. Use the inventory callbacks that Luanti provides.
  • Hypertext. Flow does not look at the markup that you give gui.Hypertext, see Hypertext markup. Escape text from players with core.hypertext_escape().

Everything in ctx except ctx.form is only changed by your code, so the client cannot change it.

docs.title: Text in elements
docs.text: Text that you put in an element, such as a label, is escaped when flow generates the formspec, so it cannot add or change other elements.

docs.title: Styling forms
docs.text:
Styles change how elements look: their colors, images, fonts, and so on. A style is a set of properties such as bgcolor = "red", and which properties exist depends on the type of element. All of them are listed in the property reference below.

You can style a single element with the style field (the inline syntax), or style many elements at once with the gui.Style and gui.StyleType elements (see separate style elements).

docs.title: Inline syntax
docs.text:
Inline styles were added in May 2024, so older versions of flow do not support this syntax, and the sub-style syntax (the sel entries) may change in the future. Only use inline styles for things that are not essential, so that your form does not look broken without them, or use separate style elements if you need to support older versions.

You can add inline styles to elements with the style field:

gui.Button {
    label = "Test",
    style = {
        bgcolor = "red",

        -- You can style specific states of elements:
        { sel = "$hovered", bgcolor = "green" },

        -- Or a combination of states:
        { sel = "$hovered, $pressed", bgcolor = "blue" },
        { sel = "$hovered+pressed", bgcolor = "white" },
    },
}

In a sel entry, $ stands for the element itself, so "$hovered+pressed" is the same as the selector "button:hovered+pressed" for an unnamed button, or "my_name:hovered+pressed" for an element named my_name. Every comma-separated entry needs its own $ (an entry without one is skipped and flow logs a warning).

The properties directly inside style always apply. A sel entry only applies while the element is in one of the listed states. Separate states with a comma to apply the style when any of them is active ("$hovered, $pressed"), or join them with + to apply it only when all of them are active at once ("$hovered+pressed").

If you need to style multiple elements, you can reuse the style table:

local my_style = { bgcolor = "red", { sel = "$hovered", bgcolor = "green" } }

local form = flow.make_gui(function(player, ctx)
    return gui.VBox {
        gui.Button { label = "Styled button", style = my_style },
        gui.Button { label = "Unstyled button" },
        gui.Button { label = "Second styled button", style = my_style },
    }
end)

Note that this may inadvertently reset styles on subsequent elements if used on elements without a name. Luanti can only style unnamed elements by their type, so flow applies the style to every element of that type and then resets those properties to their defaults straight after the element. This also undoes any earlier gui.StyleType for the same properties. Give the element a name to avoid this.

Property values are normally strings, but flow also accepts numbers and booleans where a property needs one. Setting a property to an empty string (bgimg = "") resets it to its default value.

docs.title: Separate style elements
docs.text:
Alternatively, you can use the gui.Style and gui.StyleType elements if you need to style a large group of elements or need to support older versions of flow:

gui.Style {
    selectors = { "btn1" },
    props = {
        bgimg = "button.png",
        border = false,
    }
},

gui.Button {
    name = "btn1",
    label = "Button",
},

The Style and StyleType elements are invisible and won't affect padding. They only affect the elements that come after them, so put them before the elements you want to style.

Warning: gui.Style and gui.StyleType do not support styles that change the element size, such as font_size for labels, buttons, and fields, and size/spacing for lists (added in March 2025). Flow only sees these properties in the inline syntax, so use that for them.

docs.title: Selectors and states
docs.text:
selectors is a list that says which elements the style applies to:

  • gui.Style selects elements by their name, so {"btn1"} styles the element with name = "btn1".
  • gui.StyleType selects elements by their type, so {"button"} styles every button that comes after it. The type is the element's name in lowercase with underscores between words, for example item_image_button for gui.ItemImageButton. Some types also style other types, see element types.
  • gui.StyleType also accepts "*", which selects every element.

A selector can end with a colon and one or more states to only style the element while it is in that state, such as "btn1:hovered" or "button:hovered+pressed" (+ means all of the states have to be active).

gui.StyleType {
    selectors = { "button", "image_button" },
    props = { textcolor = "yellow" },
},
gui.StyleType {
    selectors = { "button:hovered" },
    props = { bgcolor = "#336699" },
},

docs.title: States
docs.text:
Every element has the default state, which is the same as not giving any state. Buttons (gui.Button, gui.ButtonExit, gui.ImageButton, gui.ItemImageButton) also have these states:

State Active when focused The button has keyboard focus hovered The mouse is over the button pressed The button is being pressed

docs.title: Element types
docs.text:
These are the types that can be styled. A type that "inherits" from another also uses the styles set for the other type, for example a style set on image also applies to animated_image.

Type Element Inherits from animated_image gui.AnimatedImage image box gui.Box button gui.Button button_exit gui.ButtonExit button checkbox gui.Checkbox dropdown gui.Dropdown field gui.Field image gui.Image image_button gui.ImageButton item_image_button gui.ItemImageButton label gui.Label list gui.List model gui.Model pwdfield gui.Pwdfield field scrollbar gui.Scrollbar tabheader gui.Tabheader table gui.Table textarea gui.Textarea textlist gui.Textlist vertlabel gui.Vertlabel label

Luanti also lists hypertip, but flow has no element for it, see Unsupported Features. gui.ItemImage has the item_image type, which only supports noclip (see Other elements). gui.ImageButtonExit and gui.ButtonURL are not in Luanti's list of types, so give them a name and style them with gui.Style or the inline syntax.

docs.title: Property reference
docs.text: Colors are described in Functional Elements, and textures are image file names. A "2D vector" is written as a string such as "1,2". Properties that only list a type of element are not valid on other elements, and an unknown property is ignored.

docs.title: All elements
docs.text: Property Description noclip Boolean. Set to true to let the element be drawn outside the area of the form. Default false.

docs.title: Text properties
docs.text:
These properties change how text looks. font and font_size are valid on buttons, labels, fields, tables, and text lists. textcolor is valid on buttons, labels, fields, and tab headers, but not on tables and text lists. The sections below show which applies where.

Property Description font Font type, a comma-separated list. Use at most one of normal (the default font) and mono (a font where every letter is the same width), and any of bold and italic. For example "mono,bold". If you only give bold or italic, normal is used. Default normal. font_size Text size. "16" sets an absolute size, "+2" and "-2" make the text 2 points larger or smaller than the default, and "*1.5" multiplies the default size by 1.5 (like em in CSS). The default is the size the player has chosen in their settings. textcolor Color of the text. Default white.

Flow can make room for bigger text in gui.Labels, buttons, and the default text of fields, but only if font_size starts with * and is set with the inline syntax (style = {font_size = "*2"}). Other values still change the text but not the size of the element. The labels above fields and checkboxes ignore font_size, and a gui.Label with a fixed h is positioned as if font_size was not set. That positioning behavior is deprecated and flow logs a warning when it detects it, so leave h out of labels that use font_size.

docs.title: Buttons
docs.text:
For gui.Button, gui.ButtonExit, gui.ImageButton, and gui.ItemImageButton. Buttons also support font, font_size, and textcolor.

Property Description alpha Boolean. Whether to draw the transparent parts of bgimg. Default true. bgcolor Color that tints the button. bgimg Texture to use as the background of the button. Default none. bgimg_middle Draws bgimg as a nine-slice. Written as a string in one of the formats "x", "x,y", or "x,y,x2,y2", which have the same meaning as middle_x, middle_y, middle_x2, and middle_y2. Also adds padding around the content of the button. border Boolean. Whether to draw the bevelled button border. Set to false to hide it. Default true. content_offset 2D vector that moves the content (text and image) of the button without resizing the button. padding Space between the edges of the button and its content, as a rectangle written in the same formats as bgimg_middle. This value is relative to bgimg_middle. It is not the same as the padding parameter of elements, which adds space outside the element and is handled by flow, see Padding. sound The name of a sound to play when the button is triggered, such as a sound file name from a mod's sounds folder without the extension. It is played at normal volume and takes no other options.

gui.ImageButton has some more properties for the picture drawn on top of the button:

Property Description fgimg The picture to draw. Default none. The texture_name and pressed_texture_name you give to the element take precedence over this. fgimg_middle Draws fgimg as a nine-slice, like bgimg_middle.

Some older properties still work but are deprecated. Use states instead: bgcolor_hovered, bgcolor_pressed, bgimg_hovered, bgimg_pressed, fgimg_hovered, and fgimg_pressed. They work like bgcolor and bgimg but only apply while the button is hovered or pressed.

docs.title: Fields and text areas
docs.text:
For gui.Field, gui.Pwdfield, and gui.Textarea. They also support font, font_size, and textcolor.

Property Description border Boolean. Set to false to hide the background and border of the text box. Default true. halign Horizontal alignment of the text: left (default), center, or right. Needs formspec version 11 (Luanti 5.17 or newer, see the version table), and flow may not be able to use it, see Unsupported Features. valign Vertical alignment of the text: top (default), center, or bottom. Needs formspec version 11 (Luanti 5.17 or newer, see the version table). Only has an effect when all of the text fits inside the element. If the text is too long (and a gui.Textarea gets a scrollbar), it is always aligned to the top so that no text is cut off. It also does not work in gui.Field, but halign does.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
For gui.Label and gui.Vertlabel: font, font_size, and textcolor.

Luanti also has halign and valign for labels, but they only apply to the area label, which flow does not have, so they do nothing here (see Unsupported Features).

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
For gui.List:

Property Description size 2D vector. The size of each slot. Default "1,1". spacing 2D vector. The space between slots. Default "0.25,0.25".

Flow uses these values to work out how big a list is, but it only understands whole numbers in them (such as "2,2" or "0,0").

docs.title: Boxes
docs.text:
For gui.Box. These properties only take effect when the box has no color of its own. The colors, bordercolors, and borderwidths properties can have one, two, or four values separated by commas (like CSS borders):

  • One value, such as "#FF0": used for all corners or borders.
  • Two values, such as "red,#FFAAFF": for the colors, the top-left and bottom-right corners, then the top-right and bottom-left corners. For the widths, the top and bottom borders, then the left and right borders.
  • Four values, such as "blue,#A0F,green,#FFFA": starting with the top-left corner (or the top border) and going clockwise.
Property Description colors Color of the corners of the box. Default black. bordercolors Color of the borders of the box. Default black. borderwidths Width of the borders in pixels, as a whole number. A negative width puts the border inside the box, a positive width puts it outside the box, and 0 draws no border. Default 0.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
For gui.Model:

Property Description bgcolor Background color of the model area.

docs.title: Read-only elements (editable)
docs.text: Luanti 5.18 (formspec version 12) added an editable property for gui.Checkbox, gui.Dropdown, gui.Field, gui.Pwdfield, and gui.Textarea. Setting it to false makes the element read-only (default true). Flow does not support it yet, because flow always uses formspec version 7, so it may do nothing or be ignored depending on the player's version of Luanti. To make a field read-only for now, handle that in your own code, for example by ignoring changes to it. See also Newer Luanti features.

docs.title: Other elements
docs.text: Element Properties gui.Checkbox sound: A sound to play when the box is ticked or unticked. gui.Dropdown sound: A sound to play when a different item is selected. gui.Tabheader sound: A sound to play when a different tab is selected. textcolor: Color of the tab text, default white. gui.Table, gui.Textlist font and font_size. The colors of a table are set with gui.TableOptions. gui.Image, gui.AnimatedImage, gui.ItemImage, gui.Scrollbar Only noclip.

docs.title: Tooltips
docs.text:
A tooltip is a small box of text that appears when the player hovers over an element.

You can add tooltips to elements using the tooltip field:

gui.Image {
    w = 2, h = 2,
    texture_name = "air.png",
    tooltip = "Air",
}

This works on elements without a name as well. In that case the tooltip covers the area of the element, and the tooltip of a named element that overlaps it takes priority.

If the areas of two unnamed elements overlap and both have a tooltip (for example in a gui.Stack, or a box with a tooltip that contains an element with its own), the one that comes first in the form wins. Flow puts each tooltip directly before its element, and Luanti shows the first area tooltip that contains the mouse pointer, so the tooltip of a box beats the tooltips of the elements inside it.

There is also a gui.Tooltip element which lets you change the background and text color of the tooltip. It refers to the element it belongs to with gui_element_name, which must be the name of that element, and it should come after that element. As with gui.Style, it is invisible and won't affect padding.

gui.VBox {
    gui.Button { name = "my_button", label = "Hover over me" },
    gui.Tooltip {
        gui_element_name = "my_button",
        tooltip_text = "Hello!",
        bgcolor = "#000000",
        fontcolor = "#FFFF00",
    },
}

Flow cannot make tooltips that show formatted text (hypertip[]) or tooltips for an arbitrary area instead of an element, see Unsupported Features.
